scope: Read-only audit of the frozen five-minute live window.
findings: One narrow last-resort catch forecast was invalidated by measured drift before its scheduled jump; every later forecast was unreachable. This is not a missed jump dispatch or native catch rejection.

The logged initial heading was still turning while the planner modeled zero-reaction straight travel. The first solve also consumed 55.7 ms. The resulting position discrepancy is directly recorded; separating native turn dynamics from solve latency requires finer execution telemetry.
The opening alignment branch was not responsible: the observed lateral gap was below its start threshold. Existing lateral recovery requested sprint before the throw.

The subsequent ground tackle dive started. One sampled position satisfies nominal directional tackle geometry, while later samples show the receiver turning away; no native tackle request/acceptance or opponent immunity/move state is logged.
No collision, drift or catch validation is weakened. No global timing or sprint threshold change is justified by this single incident.
limitations: Planner scalar replay is not native physics or server confirmation.
A nominal tackle envelope overlap does not prove a server-accepted tackle.
Opponent turns after a committed dive are not known when the dive is chosen.
privacy: No player names, account identifiers, credentials, extracted source, or machine paths.
